plain: How much memory the game needs on each kind of computer, release by release, against the limit each one can give it. Solid lines and filled dots are measurements. Hollow dots are estimates, and dashed lines with diamonds are planned work, each tied to the change that should get it there. Open "Every point" under a chart for the build, machine, method, number of runs and date behind each value. A GB here is 1,000 MB, as the measurement reports write it.

d3d11-v3.label: memory.mts v3, Windows
d3d11-v3.device: Windows PC with an NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X, Chrome on Direct3D 11 (30 GB visible to the browser)
d3d11-v3.method: memory.mts v3: 1600x900, seed 42, Auto quality, the kong standing still through two 30-second matches. The whole browser is read from the operating system every 15 s and the game's own WebGL and copy counters at each phase. Median of interleaved runs.

d3d11-trace.label: growth trace, Windows
d3d11-trace.device: Windows PC with an NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X, Chrome on Direct3D 11 (30 GB visible to the browser)
d3d11-trace.method: Growth trace: Chrome started on its own and attached over CDP, 1600x900, seed 42, a bot walking a fixed route to the results screen, sampled every 5 s. The page was read with page.evaluate, which can add some memory, so compare it only with its own control run.

metal-chrome-v3.label: memory.mts v3, Mac Chrome
metal-chrome-v3.device: Mac mini, Apple M4, 16 GB, macOS 27, Chrome 154 on Metal
metal-chrome-v3.method: memory.mts v3: 1600x900, seed 42, Auto quality, the kong standing still through two 60-second matches. Whole browser read every 15 s, game counters at each phase. Median of 6 runs.

metal-chrome-flight.label: flight check, Mac Chrome
metal-chrome-flight.device: Mac mini, Apple M4, 16 GB, macOS 27, Chrome 154 on Metal
metal-chrome-flight.method: Flight check harness (gpu-match), headed Chrome, seed 42. WebGL is the game's textures plus buffers from the memory probe at the title and 8 s into the plane.

safari-baseline.label: first Safari baseline
safari-baseline.device: Mac mini, Apple M4, 16 GB, macOS 27, Safari 27
safari-baseline.method: Cold Safari start, prod build, seed 42, 3 runs per build. Memory as Activity Monitor counts it (footprint). Every run reached Safari's limit on this 16 GB Mac, so the value is the size at the title.

safari-acceptance.label: Safari acceptance
safari-acceptance.device: Mac mini, Apple M4, 16 GB, macOS 27, Safari 27
safari-acceptance.method: Safari acceptance: cold start, prod build, seed 42, low-memory mode on (Safari's default), the kong left standing, a full match. Value is the highest page-process (WebContent) footprint; the whisker spans the 3 runs.
safari-acceptance.source: KONG-54's acceptance report to the Captain, 2026-11-05

safari-trace.label: Safari growth trace
safari-trace.device: Mac mini, Apple M4, 16 GB, macOS 27, Safari 27
safari-trace.method: Safari growth trace: prod build, seed 42, low-memory mode on (Safari's default), an autopilot that drops and runs between locations, footprint sampled every 5 s until the results screen or until Safari closes the tab. WebGL and copy counters come from the memory probe injected before the game's scripts.

safari-gate.label: Safari release check
safari-gate.device: Mac mini, Apple M4, 16 GB, macOS 27, Safari 27.0.1
safari-gate.method: Release check on the Mac: prod build of the tag, seed 42, Auto quality (it picked Low), the moving autopilot through a full match to the results screen, peak footprint per phase. v0.6 ran at the display's own pixel ratio of 1; from v1.0 the check forces a Retina pixel ratio of 2, which draws more pixels, so v1.0 is not lower because of that.
safari-gate.source: Kong Mini's release checks (renders/v060, v061, v100, v101 in its drive), as reported to the Captain

plan.label: estimate or plan
plan.device: Worked out from the measurements named in the note
plan.method: Estimate or plan, not a measurement. The note gives the arithmetic and its sources.
plan.source: docs/memory-architecture.md, Captain drive reports/KONG-44, KONG-47 and KONG-62

mem-12gb.label: whole-browser flight, Mac mini (RAY-227)
mem-12gb.device: Mac mini, Apple M4, 16 GB, macOS 27.0.1, Chrome 154.0.8037.57 on Metal, Safari 27.0.1
mem-12gb.method: Prod build of fork main 0c1713f on a local server, DPR 1 at a 1080p surface, Auto quality, seed 42, the moving autopilot (v7) from the drop to the results screen, a full practice match per run. n=2 per arm, interleaved, each in a fresh browser process. Arm A is the defaults, arm B adds ?lowmem=1&geofree=1&farimp=1; both add &resaudit. Chrome is the sum of footprint over the Chrome process tree from the automation browser's main process; Safari is WebContent (max) and whole Safari (Safari, WebContent and WebKit GPU processes). Sampled every 2.5 s, peak kept. Notes: the first Chrome pass sampled the wrong process and was discarded and rerun; the Metal shader cache was not wiped between runs; the Mac also runs other work, so the operating system share (below) is an upper bound.
mem-12gb.source: project drive: handoffs/mem-12gb (RAY-227), measured by KONG-54

skus.name: Mac with 16 GB
skus.plain: Measured on a Mac mini with an M4 chip and 16 GB, in Safari and in Chrome. Since v0.6 a full match finishes in Safari: the game now keeps at most four streamed locations at a time, and Safari's page peaks about 1.3 GB under Safari's limit.

charts.title: Peak memory in a match
charts.measure: The highest memory seen from launch to the end of the match. For Safari, the page process (WebContent) is the number Safari watches, and the whole browser adds Safari's graphics process. For Chrome it is every Chrome process together.
charts.caption: v0.2.0 is the shared starting point of both projects. The fork set out to fit a full Safari match inside the limit Safari sets on a 16 GB Mac, and from v0.6 the match fits: across the checks the page peaked between 6.8 and 7.7 GB against a limit of about 8.4 GB (one v0.6.1 run on a longer route reached 8.3 GB and still finished). Main at 0c1713f was measured in both browsers, two runs each way. In Chrome the low-memory setup cuts the peak from 10.9 to 8.0 GB at 60 fps. In Safari the flags change nothing measurable, because Safari already runs the low-memory path. Chrome doesn't close tabs this way, so its line shows how much it asks of the Mac. The main points use a pixel ratio of 1, the v1.0 Safari point forced 2, so the two aren't a like-for-like change.

skus.name: Mac with 12 GB or 10 GB
skus.plain: Not measured on a 12 GB or 10 GB Mac. The game's footprint is the same whatever the Mac has, so this chart sets the 16 GB Mac mini's measurements against how much a smaller Mac would have left for the browser. That headroom is an estimate: the operating system's share was read from the Mini's own idle state, 6.1 to 8.1 GB, median 6.5 GB. It is an upper bound for the system's share, because the Mini was also running other work and about 2 GB of swap. A clean system was not measured.

charts.title: Peak memory against estimated headroom for 12 GB and 10 GB
charts.measure: The 16 GB Mac mini's peaks from the chart above (n=2 each, main at 0c1713f). Only the headroom lines are estimated: 12 GB less the 6.5 GB median system share is 5.5 GB, and 10 GB less it is 3.5 GB. If a smaller Mac's system share were about 3.5 GB (a rough figure that was not measured), headroom would be 8.5 GB and 6.5 GB, Chrome's low-memory setup (8.0 GB) and Safari (8.0 to 8.2 GB on defaults; 7.5 to 8.8 GB with the flags, where one run is over) would fit on 12 GB with 0.5 GB or less to spare (Safari's lowest run, 7.5 GB, would leave 1.0 GB), and nothing would fit on 10 GB. On a real small Mac the system would compress and swap and the footprints would shrink somewhat, so this shows how close the game is, not what a player would see.
charts.caption: At the measured system share, nothing fits without swapping. Chrome's low-memory setup (8.0 GB) is over by 2.5 GB on 12 GB and 4.5 GB on 10 GB; Safari's whole browser (8.0 to 8.8 GB) is over by 2.0 to 3.3 GB on 12 GB. Fitting 12 GB takes about 2.5 GB less than Chrome's low-memory setup, and 10 GB about 4.5 GB less; with 1 GB to spare, about 3.5 GB and 5.5 GB. Memory pressure reached "warn" in both Chrome defaults runs and all four Safari runs, and stayed normal in both Chrome low-memory runs.

skus.name: Phones and tablets
skus.plain: Not supported yet. Since v0.6.1, phones and tablets get a "desktop only for now" screen with a button to copy the link, shown before the game loads so the tab never runs out of memory (#195). A phone version needs two things: the game under about 1.2 GB at its peak (an estimate from WebKit's limits on iPhone, about a quarter of today's Safari page at the title) and touch controls, which the game doesn't have yet.
